{{Quote|To keep droids disciplined I need escaped droids destroyed before they exit system.|[[EV-9D9/Legends|EV-9D9]]|<ref name="SWG:Runaways" />}}
'''R3-B57''' was an [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3-series astromech droid]] that operated during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], R3-B57 served [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's]] [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] under Jabba's sadistic [[EV-series supervisor droid/Legends|EV-series supervisor droid]] [[EV-9D9/Legends|EV-9D9]]. In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline" /> R3-B57 and three other droids, [[BD-34]], [[RA-316]] and [[LIN-34]], escaped [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] and took refuge within the [[Darklighter cache]]. EV-9D9 thus hired a spacer to track down the droids to the cave. According to EV-9D9's punitive instructions, the spacer planted pain bolts to the droids before destroying them. In the meantime, Jabba's enemies of the [[Valarian Syndicate]] assigned a group of [[M12-L Kimogila heavy fighter]]s to exfiltrate R3-B57 out of the system but the ships were destroyed by Jabba's pilots in the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatooine system]].<ref name="SWG:Runaways" />

==Behind the scenes==
R3-B57 appeared as a non-player character in the video game Star Wars Galaxies, a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game developed by [[Sony]] and published by LucasArts,<ref name="SWG:Runaways" /> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> R3-B57 was added to the game as part of the "[[W:c:swg:Legacy Quest|Legacy Quest]]" with the release of the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15, 2005|Publish 25]]," a.k.a. the "[[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]]," on [[November 15]], [[2005]].<ref name="SonyCite-Publish Archive 2005">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref>
